examples.title: Basic
examples.description: Click the target or drop a file on it. `accept` limits the types, and the chosen file shows as a row you can remove.

examples.title: Multiple files
examples.description: `multiple` keeps a list. A file added twice is listed once.

examples.title: Controlled
examples.description: Pass `value` and `onFilesChange` to own the list of `File` objects.

examples.title: Accepted types
examples.description: `accept` takes extensions (`.csv`) and MIME types (`image/*`). With MIME types only, the target turns red while a file of another type is dragged over it; extensions can only be checked on drop.

examples.title: Size limit
examples.description: `maxSize` (bytes) refuses larger files. `onReject` receives the reason and the file, and the same message shows under the target.

examples.title: Maximum files
examples.description: `maxFiles` caps the list. Files over the cap are refused with a message and reported to `onReject`.

examples.title: Uploads with progress
examples.description: `onUpload` runs for each added file. Call `onProgress(0-100)` to fill the bar, resolve when the file has landed and the row turns to Uploaded with a drawn check.

examples.title: Failure and retry
examples.description: Reject with an `Error` and its message becomes the reason on the row, with a Retry pill that starts the upload again from zero. The border tints and the row shakes once.

examples.title: Cancelling
examples.description: Removing a row aborts the `signal` you were given, so you can stop the request.

examples.title: Earlier uploads
examples.description: `defaultItems` shows rows that already have a status, such as files uploaded in a previous visit. They are not part of `value` or `onFilesChange`.

examples.title: Image thumbnails
examples.description: Image files get a 40px thumbnail from an object URL that is released when the row goes. Other types get an icon for their kind.

examples.title: Drop label and note
examples.description: `dropLabel` replaces the prompt while files are over the target, and `note` replaces the line with the accepted types and size. A faint light follows the pointer along the edge while you drag.

examples.title: Compact prompt
examples.description: `compactAt` folds the prompt to a slim bar once the list holds that many rows, so the list has room. A drag over it brings the prompt back.

examples.title: Paste
examples.description: Files on the clipboard, such as a screenshot, are added while the pointer is over the component or focus is inside it. Text fields keep their own paste.

examples.title: Keyboard
examples.description: The target is a native button. Inside the list each row has one action tab stop, the arrows move between rows, and Delete removes the focused row; focus moves to a neighbouring row afterwards.

examples.title: Error
examples.description: `error` shows a message under the target, turns the edge red and sets `aria-invalid` on the input.

examples.title: Disabled
examples.description: A disabled upload cannot be opened, dropped on or pasted into.
